entries.name: Neobotics
entries.label: nonprofit
entries.what: A Massachusetts nonprofit. Its NeoRacer is an open autonomous race car for high schools and colleges, sold ready to run.
entries.origin: The NeoRacer is built to RoboRacer race rules. Neobotics co-organized the 30th RoboRacer competition, at VTC 2026 in Boston.

logo.source: https://neobotics.org/images/logos/neobotics/neobotics-icon-red.webp (the partner wall now uses the wordmark instead, Cedric 2026-09-28)

car.alt: The NeoRacer: a black race car with orange wheels, a rear wing and a lidar on top, in a dark studio with smoke
car.name: NeoRacer

preview.alt: The neobotics.org homepage further down: their vision line, then a red panel reading 'NEO RACER' beside the car, black with red wheels, lidar and rear wing

evidence.says: Neobotics Foundation incorporated Feb 26, 2025 as a Massachusetts nonprofit; 501(c)(3) in June 2025; first NeoRacer kits shipped Aug 2026; hosting an autonomous racing event with RoboRacer at IEEE VTC2026-Fall. Founders and several advisors are Boston University people.
NeoRacer product page: aimed at high schools and colleges; lists 'Compatible with Roboracer AI'.

NeoRacer paper (Bandyopadhyay, Mehta, El Mabsout, Mancuso; Jul 29, 2026): open hardware (CERN-OHL-S v2) and software (GPLv3); 'fully compatible with the F1Tenth autonomous racing ecosystem and competition rules'; the VTC 2026 event is co-organised with the RoboRacer Foundation; a school-to-college pathway is co-designed with the RoboRacer Foundation.
30th Roboracer Autonomous Racing Competition, VTC2026-Fall, Boston, Sep 6-9, 2026. Organizers: Rahul Mangharam, Ahmad Amine, Koneshka Bandyopadhyay (Founder & CEO, Neobotics Foundation Inc.).

Context only, not used in the copy: the BU F1TENTH Autonomous Grand Prix, Nov 22, 2024, was organized by Boston University faculty incl. Renato Mancuso (now a Neobotics advisor and NeoRacer co-author) with Rahul Mangharam.

entries.note: Source: Cedric, 2026-09-24 (named Neobotics as a spinoff), alongside the first-party pages in evidence. No public page says Neobotics grew out of RoboRacer; the sourced link is the rules compatibility and the VTC 2026 co-organization. If the founders came out of the BU F1TENTH Grand Prix (Nov 2024) or the BU F1TENTH student club, say so and the origin line can carry it. Cedric, 2026-09-25: show their car, logo and a preview of their website; the logo, car photo and homepage capture come from neobotics.org at his direction (permission: Cedric-directed; Neobotics not yet asked). The NeoRacer paper (arXiv 2607.26855) carries arXiv's non-exclusive licence, not CC BY, so no figure is taken from it.

entries.what: An engineering education company. Its Self-Driving Car Studio is built around the QCar 2, a 1/10-scale research car.
entries.origin: A commercial research car in the same class. Not affiliated with RoboRacer.

evidence.says: Based in Warsaw, Poland. Team: Łukasz and Monika Sztyber. Started in 2018 with the Udacity Self-Driving Car Engineer nanodegree; raced F1TENTH, now RoboRacer, indoors at robotics conferences ('F1TENTH / RoboRacer · 2018 to 2024', six podiums: 1st IROS 2024 Abu Dhabi, 2nd ICRA 2024 Yokohama, 2nd ADAC event 2022 Lausitzring, 2nd ICRA 2022 Philadelphia, 1st ES Week 2019 New York, 1st ES Week 2018 Turin). Since 2025 ('Human vs AI'): the cars race in the 1/8 RC class against a professional human driver, indoors or out, on asphalt. Cars Dzik1 and Dzik2 on a PlatformSworkz S35-GT2E chassis with a custom carbon frame.

'2026.10.04 | Autonomous Racing | Ruda Śląska | track perspective (center)', channel Dzik Autonomous Racing (@dzik.racing), 26 s, 1920x1080, uploaded 2026-10-07, public and embeddable. A trackside camera follows one small car around an outdoor asphalt RC track.

candidates.name: ForzaETH Race Stack
candidates.what: ETH Zurich's open-source software for head-to-head racing on the RoboRacer car, built for off-the-shelf parts.
candidates.origin: The ForzaETH student team wrote it to race RoboRacer competitions, won several, then released the whole stack in 2024.

evidence.says: ForzaETH Race Stack paper (Mar 2024, Journal of Field Robotics): an autonomous racing software platform designed for F1TENTH on commercial off-the-shelf hardware; it won the official F1TENTH international competition multiple times.
Repo by ETH Zurich's D-ITET Center for Project Based Learning; builds on f1tenth_system, the F1TENTH simulator and the f1tenth vesc driver.

candidates.note: A product that came out of racing the car. Keep, or is ForzaETH better shown as a team?

candidates.name: RoboRacer Sim Racing League
candidates.what: An online league where teams race a digital twin of the RoboRacer car in the AutoDRIVE simulator, no car needed.
candidates.origin: Clemson's AutoDRIVE team started it with RoboRacer organizers at IROS 2024; it has run at CDC, ICRA and IROS since.

evidence.says: The first RoboRacer Sim Racing League, at IROS 2024, on AutoDRIVE digital twins; organizers include Rahul Mangharam, Venkat Krovi, Johannes Betz, Chinmay and Tanmay Samak, Ahmad Amine, Hongrui Zheng.
Editions listed: IROS 2024, CDC 2024, ICRA 2025, CDC-TF 2025, ICRA 2026, IROS 2026.
RoboRacer Digital Twin Autonomous Sim-Racing League using AutoDRIVE Ecosystem (successor of the 2024 F1TENTH Sim Racing repo).

candidates.note: Co-run with RoboRacer, so arguably part of RoboRacer rather than a spinoff. Keep it here, or move it to Race?

candidates.name: Cavalier Autonomous Racing
candidates.what: The University of Virginia's full-size autonomous racing team, the first American team to win the Indy Autonomous Challenge.
candidates.origin: Founded by F1TENTH co-founder Madhur Behl. Most of its first members had worked on F1TENTH cars for five years.

evidence.says: Behl is founder and team principal of UVA's Cavalier Autonomous Racing, the first American team to win the Indy Autonomous Challenge; he co-founded the F1Tenth platform and its Grand Prix competitions.
IAC team profile: the majority of team members had been involved in F1/10 autonomous racing development for the past 5 years.

candidates.note: The clearest 'grew out of F1TENTH' story in the public record. The team's founding year is not on either page.
